title: Shell Navigation Basics
description: Learn essential shell commands for navigating the file system

steps.title: Understanding the File System
steps.content:
The file system is organized in a tree-like structure of directories (folders) and files. Important concepts:

- Root directory (/): The top-level directory
- Home directory (~): Your user's home folder
- Current directory (.): The directory you're in
- Parent directory (..): The directory above current

Paths can be:
- Absolute (starting from root): /Users/username/Documents
- Relative (from current location): ./documents

steps.title: Basic Navigation Commands
steps.content:
Essential commands for moving around:

- pwd: Print Working Directory (shows where you are)
- ls: List directory contents
- cd: Change Directory

Common usage:
- cd ~ (go to home)
- cd .. (go up one level)
- cd /path/to/directory (go to specific location)

practical_task.description: Navigate to your home directory, then list its contents. Type 'done' when completed.

steps.title: Listing Files and Directories
steps.content:
The ls command has useful options:

- ls -l: Long format (detailed info)
- ls -a: Show hidden files
- ls -h: Human-readable sizes
- ls -R: Recursive listing

Combine options: ls -lah (long format, all files, human-readable)

practical_task.description: List all files (including hidden) in long format with human-readable sizes. What command did you use?

steps.title: Working with Paths
steps.content:
Understanding paths is crucial:

- Absolute paths start with /
- Relative paths are from current location
- ~ represents home directory
- . represents current directory
- .. represents parent directory

Example: cd ../Documents moves up one level then into Documents

exercises.question: What symbol represents the home directory?
exercises.explanation: The tilde (~) is a shortcut for your home directory.

exercises.question: What command shows your current location?
exercises.explanation: pwd (Print Working Directory) shows the full path of your current location.

exercises.question: What ls option shows hidden files?
exercises.explanation: ls -a shows all files, including hidden ones that start with a dot.

exercises.question: What symbol represents the parent directory?
exercises.explanation: Two dots (..) refers to the directory one level up from your current location.
